claim: The maximum number of unit distances among n pairwise 1-separated points in the plane (the maximum edge count of an n-vertex penny graph) equals floor(3n - sqrt(12n-3)), and at the centred hexagonal numbers n = 3k^2+3k+1 this evaluates exactly to 9k^2+3k, attained by the hexagonal patch of the triangular lattice.

facets.entities: finite point sets in the Euclidean plane with all pairwise distances at least 1 (penny graphs / minimum-distance graphs)
facets.mechanism: convex-hull boundary vertices have deficient unit-degree; the sqrt(12n-3) term is the isoperimetric penalty of the hull
facets.method: induction on the number of vertices removing a hull vertex of unit-degree at most 3; explicit hexagonal triangular-lattice patch for sharpness
facets.outcome: maximum number of unit-distance pairs e(n) = floor(3n - sqrt(12n-3)); exactly 9k^2+3k at n = 3k^2+3k+1
